abstract.p: An antenna structure and a method of forming an antenna on a conductive carrier are claimed and disclosed. The structure includes a carrier (18) having an electricity conductive surface (18.1) and a magnetic field interacting layer (20) including an amorphous or nanocrystalline magnetic material alloy, such as VITROPERM 500 F<TM>, provided on or near the surface. In use, the antenna structure is driven with a signal source generating a frequency in the band 1 MHz to 3000 MHz.

L'invention se rapporte à une structure d'antenne et à un procédé de fabrication d'une antenne sur un support conducteur. Ladite structure comporte un support (18) doté d'une surface électriquement conductrice (18.1) et une couche (20) interagissant avec le champ magnétique et comportant un alliage de matières magnétiques amorphes ou nanocristallines, du type VITROPERM 500 F<TM>, disposée sur ou à proximité de ladite surface. En cours d'utilisation, la structure d'antenne est commandée par une source de signaux générant une fréquence dans la bande 1 MHz à 3000 MHz.

description.p: CONFORMAL ANTENNA
TECHNICAL FIELD
THIS invention relates to radio frequency antennas and more
particularly to conformal antennas for use on a vehicle or craft, such
as an aeroplane or helicopter.
BACKGROUND ART
A conformal antenna conforms to the shape of a carrier body, such as
that of a vehicle or craft. They are used in practice to form a large
enough antenna on the carrier to cover a desired frequency range
and/or to reduce air resistance and/or for aesthetical reasons. For
example, in the case of an aeroplane, the antenna may be formed to
include at least parts of the metallic skinned fuselage and/or at least
one metallic skinned wing of the aeroplane.
However, a conformal antenna requires regions of high impedance in
some areas of the metallic carrier surface. This may be achieved by
physically interrupting or slotting the carrier body or skin in such areas.
Such a construction is not desirable, because in most situations the

carrier is weakened.
OBJECT OF THE INVENTION
Accordingly it is an object of the present invention to provide an
antenna structure and a method of forming same with which the
applicant believes the aforementioned disadvantages may at least be
alleviated.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
According to the invention there is provided an antenna structure
including a carrier having a conductive surface and a layer of magnetic
field interacting means applied on or near a region of the surface, to
inhibit flow of electrical current in the surface across the region.
The magnetic field interacting means serves to interact with magnetic
fields associated with surface currents to suppress those currents.
The magnetic field interacting means may be an amorphous or
nanocrystalline magnetic material alloy, preferably an amorphous or
nanocrystalline magnetic metal alloy. An example of a suitable alloy is
VITROPERM 500 F ™ which is a Fe-based alloy (Fe73.5 Cu 1 Nb3

SM 5.5 B7) .
The carrier may be a vehicle, such as a motor vehicle or craft, such as
an aeroplane or helicopter having metallic skinned wings or fuselages.
The magnetic field interacting means may be applied on the carrier to
form a slot, loop or dipole antenna, for example.
According to another aspect of the invention there is provided a
method of forming an antenna on a conductive carrier, the method
including the steps of providing a layer of magnetic field interacting
means on a region of the carrier, to inhibit flow of electrical current in
the carrier across the region.
The magnetic field interacting means may be a suitable amorphous or
nanocrystalline magnetic material alloy, preferably a magnetic metal
alloy.
The material may be provided in the form of a tape and the layer may
thus be provided by applying the tape on the surface in a linear form

or by wrapping it around a region of the carrier.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE ACCOMPANYING DIAGRAMS
The invention will now further be described, by way of example only,
with reference to the accompanying diagrams wherein
figure 1 is a plan view of an aeroplane including an antenna
structure according to the invention;
figure 2 is a section on line II in figure 1 ;
figure 3 shows an alternative configuration for the antenna
structure;
figure 4 is a diagrammatic perspective view of yet another
alternative antenna structure according to the invention;
and
figure 5 is a diagram of a dipole antenna which is equivalent to
the structure in figure 4.
DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS OF THE INVENTION
An aeroplane including a conformal antenna structure 1 0 according to
the invention is generally designated by the reference numeral 1 2 in
figure 1 .
The aeroplane body includes a fuselage 1 4 and wings 1 6 and 1 8, each
covered with an electricity conductive metallic skin. The skin 1 8.1 of

wing 1 8 is shown in better detail in figure 2.
The conformal antenna structure 10 conforms to the shape of the
body of its carrier, namely the aeroplane wing. It is formed by
applying a layer 20 of a magnetic field interacting means in the form
of an amorphous or nanocrystalline metal alloy in suitable regions on
the body, effectively to create on the metallic surface high impedance
regions, thereby to create a suitable surface mounted antenna
geometry or pattern on the body.
The magnetic field interacting means may be the product VITROPERM
500 F™ which is a Fe-based alloy (Fe73.5 Cu1 Nb3 Si1 5.5 B7).
The layer 20 on the conductive wing 18 is shown in more detail in
figure 2. The layer 20 interacts with magnetic fields associated with
electrical current to suppress the current in the skin below the layer,
with the result that electronically speaking a slot is emulated in region
a of the antenna, separating feed point regions 22 and 24 from one
another. By the provision of such layers on the fuselage and/or
wings, the flow of current in the metallic skin can be controlled.
Should an RF source 26 generating a frequency in the range 1 MHz to

3000MHz be connected to the feed point regions, the result would be
that a conformal antenna (which may be a large dipole antenna, a slot
antenna or the like) is formed at these frequencies.
The magnetic field interacting means may be provided in the form of a
tape or the like to facilitate application thereof on the wing and on or
around selected regions of the fuselage.
In figure 3 there is shown another antenna structure according to the
invention. The magnetic field interacting means 30 is applied in the
form of a ring on the conductive carrier 32. When driven as shown,
the structure yields a substantially omnidirectional antenna. The
polarization of the antenna is perpendicular to the plane of the carrier
In figure 4 there is shown yet another antenna structure 40. The
structure includes a hollow or solid rod 42 of an electricity conductive
material. The magnetic field interacting means is provided in the form
of a body 44 in a centre region of the rod. The body 44 is formed by
winding a tape 46 of the magnetic field interacting material on itself.
The tape is wound directly onto the rod or an air gap 47 may be

provided between the rod and the body. When driven by an RF
source 48 on either side of the body 44, a dipole antenna is formed.
The equivalent dipole antenna 50 is shown in figure 5.
It will be appreciated that there are many variations in detail on the
antenna structure and method of forming same according to the
invention without departing from the scope and spirit of the appended
claims.

claim.claim-text: CLAIMS
1 . An antenna structure including a carrier having an electricity
conductive surface; and a body of magnetic field interacting
means mounted on or near a region of the surface, to inhibit
flow of electrical current in the surface across the region.
2. An antenna structure as claimed in claim 1 wherein the
magnetic field interacting means includes an amorphous or
nanocrystalline magnetic material alloy.
3. An antenna structure as claimed in claim 2 wherein the
magnetic material alloy is a magnetic metal alloy.
4. An antenna structure as claimed in claim 3 wherein the
magnetic metal alloy includes VITROPERM 500 F™.
5. An antenna structure as claimed in any one of the preceding

claims wherein the surface is substantially planar and wherein
the body is in the form of at least one layer superimposed on
the surface.
6. An antenna structure as claimed in claim 5 wherein the layer is
of elongate configuration.
7. An antenna structure as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 4
wherein the surface is substantially planar and the body is of
annular configuration.
8. An antenna structure as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 4
wherein the carrier is of elongate configuration, wherein the
body is of annular configuration and provided co-axially with the
carrier, in a centre region thereof.
9. An antenna structure as claimed in claim 8 wherein the carrier is
a rod and the body includes a tape of the material coiled on
itself.
10. An antenna structure as claimed in any one of the preceding

claims including a signal source for generating a frequency
between 1 MHz and 3000MHz connected to the carrier on
opposite sides of the body.
1 1 . A method of forming an antenna on a conductive carrier
including the steps of providing a layer of magnetic field
interacting means on or near a region of the carrier.
12. A method as claimed in claim 1 1 wherein the magnetic field
interacting means includes an amorphous or nanocrystalline
magnetic material alloy.
1 3. A method as claimed in claim 1 2 wherein the magnetic material
alloy includes a magnetic metal alloy.
1 4. A method as claimed in claim 1 3 wherein the magnetic metal
alloy includes VITROPERM 500 F™.
1 5. A vehicle including a body at least part of which includes an
electricity conductive surface; and an antenna structure at or
near the surface, the antenna structure including a body of

magnetic field interacting means mounted on or near a region of
the surface, to inhibit flow of electrical current in the surface
across the region.
6. An antenna structure substantially as herein described with
reference to the accompanying diagrams.
7. A method of forming an antenna on a conductive carrier
substantially as herein described with reference to the
accompanying diagrams.
8. A vehicle or craft substantially as described with reference to
the accompanying diagrams.
